entries.topic: Falwell, the Moral Majority and Begin's outreach

claims.text: Falwell and Paul Weyrich founded the Moral Majority in June 1979; Weyrich coined the name; Viguerie, Dolan and Phillips urged Falwell to found it; it drew on the Old Time Gospel Hour mailing list; it claimed more than four million members and two million donors at its height; Falwell disbanded it in 1989 citing cash-flow problems ('Our goal has been achieved'). The article does not mention Israel.

Balmer (Politico, 27 May 2014) argued the religious right's real roots lay in defence of segregated Christian schools against IRS action after Green v. Connally (Bob Jones), quoting Weyrich (1990): 'I was trying to get these people interested in those issues and I utterly failed.' Israel does not figure in his account.
Whitehead (TGC, 8 Aug 2022) disputed Balmer: the trigger was the IRS's 1978 proposed rules on church schools (about 150,000 letters), not segregation per se; abortion was one of several streams.

Falwell received the Jabotinsky Centennial Medal in 1980, one of 100 Americans honoured by the Jabotinsky Foundation of New York; Begin presented the medals at a dinner in New York in November 1980; Senator Frank Church declined the award in protest at its also going to Falwell.

In 1979 Falwell and other pastors, invited by the National Religious Broadcasters, travelled to Israel, Jordan and Egypt and met Begin, Sadat and King Hussein; Falwell visited Israel about 15 times; in January 1999 he led 1,500 people to Israel; Liberty's account calls the 1980 award an Israeli government award (the encyclopedic record says it was given by the Jabotinsky Foundation and presented by Begin).
Rabbi Marc Tanenbaum (Sept 1981) criticised Begin for meeting only Falwell on his US visit, 'in effect' ignoring 50 million Catholics, calling the 'repeated singling out of Rev. Falwell' a mistake.

JTA (7 Mar 1985): Peres received Falwell reluctantly, aides barred photographers; Falwell said 'We are for Israel and not for the (Labor) Alignment or the Likud'; he phoned Begin; Arens addressed 850 delegates of Falwell's 'Friendship Journey to Israel-85'; he met Shamir and Sharon; mainstream American Jewish organisations objected to his social positions.

claims.text: ICEJ says it was founded in September 1980 after the Knesset declared reunited Jerusalem Israel's capital, Arab oil states threatened an embargo, and the last 13 embassies moved to Tel Aviv; it calls its work a 'ministry of comfort' (Isaiah 40:1-2) and aims at 'pro-active expressions of Christian support for Israel in every nation on earth'.
ICEJ founded 1980 by evangelical Christians in response to the Jerusalem Law and embassy closures; its Feast of Tabernacles draws several thousand from almost 100 countries; headed by Jurgen Buhler.

Bridges for Peace, Jerusalem-based, founded by Dr. Douglas Young; marked its 50th year in 2015; describes 'unconditional friendship to Israel'; serves the needy, counters antisemitism; donated ambulances to Magen David Adom; president Rebecca Brimmer.

Yechiel Eckstein founded IFCJ in 1983, raised 'hundreds of millions of dollars' mostly from Christians; in 2014 IFCJ started its own aliyah operation with a $1,000 grant per immigrant after Jewish Agency funding stopped; in 2001 Chief Rabbi Avraham Shapira condemned use of Christian money; Rabbi Elyashiv forbade cooperation as 'close to idolatry'; Eckstein died February 2019 aged 67; daughter Yael was global executive vice-president.

IFCJ (EIN 36-3256096, Chicago) Form 990 total revenue: $106.7m (2011), $132.8m (2015), $118.1m (2019), $157.6m (2020), $219.9m (2021), $227.6m (2022), $271.5m (2023), $318.2m (2024, of which contributions $307.5m; expenses $272.0m); Yael Eckstein-Farkas president & CEO from 2020 filings.

entries.topic: CUFI: founding, membership claims, summits, lobbying, disclosure, positions

claims.text: CUFI: originally established 1975 by David A. Lewis; relaunched by Hagee and incorporated 7 Feb 2006 with 'over 400 pastors and ministry leaders'; David Brog founding executive director until April 2018; Diana Hagee and Shari Dollinger then co-executive directors; membership milestones: 1m (Mar 2012), 2m (Jan 2015), 5.1m (Dec 2018); intro claims 'over 10 million'; Wikipedia lists it as a 501(c)(4) with Tax ID 46-1868892 (the Action Fund's EIN); official stance against proselytising.
CUFI announced on 22 December 2020 that it had passed 10 million members; no definition of membership given in the report.

JVL: CUFI claimed over 7m members in 2019 and over 10m in 2023; says Action Fund established 2020 (contradicted by Action Fund 990-EZ filings from 2013); lists positions: aid and QME, opposing pressure for concessions, Iran sanctions, IHRA definition, anti-BDS laws, Taylor Force Act, Golan recognition; Hagee says Christian Zionists support Israel out of gratitude, not to convert Jews; quote 'eternal covenant between God and the seed of Abraham'.
Pence at CUFI's 12th summit, 17 July 2017: CUFI 'more than 3.3 million believers'; 'my passion for Israel springs from my Christian faith'; on embassy 'It is not a question of if, it is only when.'

Pence at CUFI summit 8 July 2019: CUFI represents '6 million'; 'She said 7 million'; recalled 'a few hundred' at start and 'more than 3 million' at his previous appearance; cited embassy move and Golan recognition.

CUFI press release 27 Nov 2018: more than 4.5 million members, nearly 110,000 in Kentucky; $100,000 two-week digital and cable ad buy and full-page newspaper ads to press Sen. Rand Paul to lift his hold on the US-Israel Security Assistance Authorization Act; Hagee: 'Sen. Paul is way outside the mainstream on this.'

CUFI Action Fund spent 'six figures' on billboards in Kentucky's 4th district before the 19 May 2026 primary ('Tell Massie: Support Peace Through Strength', 'No Support for Iranian Regime'); Ari Morgenstern: aim to secure 'every available billboard in the district'.
2014 CUFI summit: 'some 4,800' delegates; lobbying day next day against PA funding; Netanyahu taped message; 2013 eighth summit: Netanyahu via satellite, Hagee 'The Holocaust ended with statehood!'

May 2008: sermon from the 1990s in which Hagee said 'Hitler was a hunter' surfaced; McCain: 'deeply offensive and indefensible, and I repudiate them'; Hagee withdrew his endorsement, saying claims he condoned the Holocaust were 'the worst of lies'; earlier that month he had apologised for remarks critics considered anti-Catholic.

claims.text: Netanyahu addressed CUFI's Washington summit of 8 July 2019 remotely, 'from Jerusalem'.
Liberty Champion: Falwell visited Israel around 15 times; in January 1999 he and Duke Westover took 1,500 people (900 Liberty students), 'the largest group to visit Israel at once'.

JTA 1985: Falwell told Peres Israel is 'the most important democracy in the area' and preserves American influence in the face of 'Soviet threats'; Falwell phoned Begin for about 15 minutes; other American Jews favour the friendship for its 'consistent support for Israel'.

JTA 2019: Eckstein died at home in Jerusalem aged 67; in a 2002 article he wrote that 'the majority of evangelicals are passionately pro-Israel because it is part of their theology' and 'I could not accept the conditional love of those who expect a payback on behalf of my people'; Jewish Agency funding stopped in 2014 'amid a fight over recognition', and Eckstein had long-held reservations about the agency's efficiency; IFCJ offered each new immigrant 'a $1,000 grant' on top of Jewish Agency benefits.
Charisma 2013: eighth annual summit; Netanyahu via satellite; 'We took Capitol Hill by storm today!' said Victor Styrsky, CUFI eastern regional director.

Jewish Press 2014: 'some 4,800' delegates; Netanyahu 'via taped message'; Lindsey Graham told Israel to 'go as far as you need to go, and do what you've got to do'; next day members lobbied to 'stop funding the Palestinian Authority'.

Jewish Insider 2026: CUFI Action Fund spending 'six figures'; billboards show Trump atop the American flag and Massie atop the Iranian flag ('Kentucky = Trump Country', 'Tell Massie: Support Peace Through Strength', 'No Support for Iranian Regime'); Ari Morgenstern, senior director of CUFI Action Fund: 'securing every available billboard in the district'.
ICEJ: a 'group of Evangelicals' founded a 'Christian Embassy' as 'an act of solidarity with the Jewish people's deep spiritual longing and attachment to this city'.
